subject: Svc boundary & interface matrix — feedback requested
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, infra@acme.com, katie.long@acme.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Svc boundary & interface matrix — feedback requested

Team / ACME infra,

Attached is the first-pass "service boundary + interface matrix" for the private deployment (control plane <-> data plane, egress, and north-south breakouts). Key asks: please review the matrix rows highlighted in yellow — those are the items we think need explicit sign-off from ACME before we lock the cutover checklist.

High-level notes:
- Control plane endpoints are pinned to the redwood-control cluster (two VIPs, active-passive).
- Data-plane worker pods sit in tenant VPCs; egress is via customer-managed NAT/GW unless ACME prefers redwood-managed egress.
- MTLS trust domains: we propose separate CA chains for control-plane and data-plane with short-lived certs.
- Proposed CIDR ranges (data-plane subnets) are in the diagram; please flag conflicts with your existing clusters.

Attachments: svc-boundary-interface-matrix_v1.pdf, network-diagram_v2.drawio.png

Please reply with: (1) any missing interfaces, (2) objections to the egress flow, (3) whether ACME can provide an ops IP-range for allowlisting.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, infra@acme.com, katie.long@acme.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Svc boundary & interface matrix — feedback requested

On Fri, 1 Jun 2028 at 09:12 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team / ACME infra,
>
> Attached is the first-pass "service boundary + interface matrix" ...

Quick pass comments (attached as jonas_comments.xlsx):
- Add explicit entry for "metrics exporter -> telemetry collector" (TCP/4317), with retry/backoff expectations.
- NAT considerations: if ACME egress uses a shared NAT, we need a sticky 5-tuple mapping doc to avoid ephemeral port exhaustion during scale-up.
- BGP / route advertisement: callout needed if ACME uses on-prem SRs to route to the redwood peering point.

Small ask: can we include a row that defines the SLA for KV cache warm-up (expected additional latency on first tenant warm-up)? That will feed the cutover plan.

Jonas
Senior Systems Engineer

From: Katie Long <katie.long@acme.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: infra@acme.com, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Svc boundary & interface matrix — feedback requested

Thanks Kimberly & team — ACME infra reviewed the attachments. A couple of constraints from our side:

- Allowlist: we can provide a /28 range for ops (will share in a follow-up note). We cannot provide a single IP for control-plane; peering will be via our transit and expect dynamic routes.
- CIDR conflict: the "tenant-subnet-2" range overlaps an existing on-prem cluster. Can you move that to 10.40.0.0/22 instead?
- Syslog/metrics: we prefer a JIT syslog-forwarder model (customer side) to avoid opening inbound ports. Are you able to support pushing logs to our collector via a secured outbound channel?

On the MTLS point — ok to use separate CA chains, but ACME requires an audit log for cert issuance; we will need a short export window (30 days) during cutover.

I'll schedule 30 minutes next week to finalize the matrix items that need sign-off.

—Katie
Cloud Platform Lead, ACME Cloud

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: katie.long@acme.com, infra@acme.com
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Svc boundary & interface matrix — feedback requested

Folks — thanks for the quick responses. Operational checklist (proposal for cutover playbook):

1) Pre-cutover (T-7 days)
   - ACME provides ops IP / transit peer details (owner: ACME infra)
   - Redlist: finalize CIDR swaps (owner: Kimberly)
   - Run a dry-run in staging: validate MTLS chain issuance and certificate rotation (owner: Neha)
2) Cutover window (T+0)
   - Update peering announcements, confirm route convergence (owner: Jonas)
   - Perform traffic-shift in 10% increments per 15-minute interval, monitor token latency and error-rate (owner: Ops)
   - Ensure syslog exporter is connected to ACME collector; fallback to s3-arch if not (owner: Neha)
3) Post-cutover (T+1 day to T+30)
   - Audit cert issuance logs and hand over 30-day export to ACME (owner: Infra Compliance)
   - Run regression prompts against live tenants (owner: Product)

Please review and add any missing owners. I want to lock this schedule by EOD Thurs so we can book change windows. Can someone volunteer to run the staging dry-run and capture a short checklist?

Irene Choi
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
